page.title: Placement Preview
page.purpose: Show a selected candidate in every placement its style declares, at desktop and mobile, so layout fitness is judged before release rather than discovered after integration.

priorities.statement: Every preview carries its own contrast verdict.
priorities.notes: A backdrop can pass as a desktop full-bleed hero and fail as a mobile crop. One verdict per candidate would hide the failure that actually ships.

priorities.statement: Previews use representative copy, not placeholder text.
priorities.notes: Headline length and weight determine whether the overlay region is adequate. Lorem would make the preview a lie.

priorities.statement: A failing placement is visibly failing, not quietly omitted.
priorities.notes: The value of this surface is catching the case that would otherwise ship.

priorities.statement: Mockup chrome fidelity is chosen by the surface, never by the operator.
priorities.notes: A product surface previews in chrome derived from the target scenario's tokens; a store surface previews inside a facsimile of the destination store. The judgements differ — 'does this belong to our product' versus 'does this hold up beside competing listings' — so the mockups must (D-010).

states.description: Placement previews reserve their geometry while candidates load.
The last placement verdicts remain visible with a freshness notice.
Placement failure names the failed render and offers retry.
Completed placement verdicts remain visible while other viewports are pending.
No candidate is selected and the surface routes to candidates.
Every declared placement renders at both viewports with a passing verdict.
A placement passes at desktop and fails at mobile. Both verdicts are shown and the failing combination is named explicitly.
A failing preview shows the computed minimum scrim alongside a before-and-after comparison, offered as an amendment rather than applied silently.
The style declares one placement. The surface renders that one without implying others were skipped.
No candidate has been selected yet. Routes back to the candidate set.
A store surface previewed inside a facsimile of its destination listing, with the device frame's footprint shown as an occlusion region rather than a gated one.
A product surface previewed in chrome derived from the target scenario's design tokens — type scale, control shapes, radii, neutrals — so the mockup reads as plausibly that product.
The candidate's produced dimensions do not match its declared surface. States expected and actual geometry and blocks release (SUR-003).
